# HTML fixture provenance

`captured_rows.html` contains four exact entry/metadata row pairs extracted
from HTML downloaded during development inspection, plus an added comment
and table wrapper. They were not generated by the synthetic fixture builder.

| Source | Captured IDs | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://news.ycombinator.com/ | 49910553, 49884346, 49909056 | Ordinary story, singular comment, `discuss` |
| https://news.ycombinator.com/jobs | 49834893 | Job spacer and age-only metadata |

Homepage capture: HTTP 200, UTF-8 HTML, 34,477 bytes, downloaded at
`2026-09-30T16:52:08.969002+00:00` (2026-10-01 in Asia/Taipei).
Full-page SHA-256:
`b7ceafa9a66f5e1a350d796846d6f2a7bd9122492adb5fa74bfeaa138dd9e4cc`.

Jobs HTML was downloaded in the same inspection session and inspected by
`2026-09-30T16:54:16.201581+00:00`.
Full-page SHA-256:
`97271162bda7cb216dddb79de3898e8d71d10b81196a7f8c8586000220341a8c`.

The homepage had no job entries. The job excerpt comes from the jobs page,
not the homepage. Tests assemble the excerpts with synthetic rows to reach
30 entries; that composite is not claimed to be a real captured homepage.
Full pages stay outside the submitted fixtures, in ignored development files.
Live titles and metrics will change; tests use these fixed excerpts offline.

All HTML produced by `story` and `page` in `test_parser.py` is synthetic,
including deliberately damaged rows. The layout mirrors observed row structure;
it does not assert that its made-up titles or item IDs were ever published.
